subject: KitePay request: temporary P1/P2 response flexibility for migration window
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@kitepay.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, support@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@kitepay.com
Date: 2026-09-15T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary response-time flexibility during KitePay DB migration (Sep 27-29)

Hi Grace —

We're planning a major database migration the weekend of Sep 27-29 that will touch several payment-related endpoints. Our infra team expects a spike in paging and transient errors while we switch traffic over; to avoid unnecessary escalations and churn we wanted to request a temporary, limited exception to our P1/P2 response requirements for that window.

Specifically we are asking:
- P1 response target to be relaxed from 30 minutes to 90 minutes during the migration windows (02:00–08:00 UTC on 2026-09-27 through 2026-09-29).
- P2 response target to be increased from 2 hours to 6 hours for the same windows.

We understand this is non-standard. Attached is our migration plan and a completed SLA change request form that outlines expected traffic and mitigations. If helpful, we can do a short sync this week to walk through the plan.

Primary contact for the migration will be Alex Mercer (alex@kitepay.com) and their ops lead Samir Patel (support@kitepay.com). Contracts copied for visibility on any formal amendment required.

Thanks — appreciate your help coordinating.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform
KitePay

Attachments: KitePay_migration_plan.pdf, SLA_change_request_form.docx
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@kitepay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, contracts@kitepay.com
Date: 2026-09-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary response-time flexibility during KitePay DB migration (Sep 27-29)

Alex —

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the migration plan. I pulled Ben (support ops) and Marcus (serving/runtime) into thread so we can triage internally quickly. A few immediate asks so we can evaluate the exception:

1) Expected increase in P1 pages per hour during the window (ballpark).
2) Are you asking for a blanket SLA doc amendment or a short-term operational carveout tied to the three dates?
3) Will KitePay accept our proposed mitigations (pre-warm dedicated capacity + temporary on-call shadowing) to minimize the time we need to relax targets?

Ben — can you confirm whether we can staff additional shadow on-call shifts for those nights and what cost/credits this would incur?
Marcus — any runtime/infra constraints on our side if we pre-warm and route KitePay traffic to a warmed pool?

If everything looks reasonable we can provisionally approve an exception limited to the three migration dates, subject to an exec sign-off and a signed amendment if contracts require it. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the migration plan? If so suggest 10:00 or 14:00 PT.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary response-time flexibility during KitePay DB migration (Sep 27-29)

Quick technical read from runtime:

- We can pre-warm a warmed GPU pool for the requested window and route KitePay traffic to it. That reduces cold-starts and KV-cache misses.
- For a conservative traffic spike estimate (2–3x normal token throughput), we'd recommend provisioning a 30% surge buffer to keep median latencies stable. I've attached a capacity ramp estimate.
- With the surge buffer + pre-warm we can realistically hold P1 median response time SLA to ~60 minutes during the busiest intervals; 90 minutes is definitely safe but we should avoid any customer-facing SLA widening unless contractual.

Operational asks:
1) If KitePay accepts the warmed pool approach, we need confirmation by EOD 2026-09-20 to reserve capacity and finalize runbooks.
2) Ben — please confirm whether on-call shadowing is doable for 02:00–08:00 UTC on each migration date and whether we want to deploy a temporary primary/secondary pager during those nights.

I can join the call tomorrow if you schedule.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_ramp_estimate.xlsx

Subject: Re: Request: temporary response-time flexibility during KitePay DB migration (Sep 27-29) — approved (provisional)

Alex / KitePay contracts team —

Thank you for the call earlier and for the detailed plan. After internal review we can provisionally approve a limited, timeboxed exception for the migration window with the following conditions:

- Timebox: 2026-09-27 02:00 UTC through 2026-09-29 08:00 UTC.
- P1: target response window relaxed to 60 minutes (we negotiated to 60m with runtime team; Marcus flagged 60m achievable with warmed pool + surge buffer).
- P2: target response window relaxed to 4 hours.
- Coverage: Redwood will provide on-call shadowing for 02:00–08:00 UTC on all three nights; primary pager during the window will be Marcus Lin, secondary ben_carter.
- Escalation path: first contact Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwood.com), then Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com), then Grace O'Connor (grace_oconnor@redwood.com).
- Operational prerequisites from KitePay: signed SLA amendment (DocuSign), final traffic estimate by 2026-09-20 EOD, and a nominated on-site ops lead reachable via phone.

Contracts: if you need a formal amendment, please route the DocuSign link to the contracts@kitepay.com address; we've placed a placeholder DocuSign packet here: https://www.docusign.com/NPQ-4892037. Once we have the signed amendment and the final traffic numbers we'll lock capacity reservations.

Next steps:
1) KitePay to confirm final traffic numbers by 2026-09-20 EOD.
2) KitePay to sign the amendment via DocuSign.
3) Redwood to reserve warmed pool and confirm the runbook; Marcus will share a short escalation runbook with names and phone numbers once capacity is reserved.

I'll convert this provisional agreement into a short addendum for signatures and drop it into HubSpot (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890).

Appreciate the partnership here — we'll do our best to keep disruptions minimal.

Regards,
